TUESDAY 6 OCTOBER 2026 – Nettle has announced an oversubscribed $4.8M Seed round led by MTech , with participation from Project A, SVV (Sure Valley Ventures), Portfolio Ventures, and Ventures Together. The round brings Nettle’s total funding to $6.8M, following its $2M pre-seed round in March 2025. Commercial insurers have a Loss Control problem: there are more risks to assess and fewer experienced risk engineers to assess them. Teams already face backlogs of up to six months, while an estimated 40% of risk engineers are expected to retire by 2030 . Nettle has built the AI Workspace for Loss Control to solve this. Its platform brings risk identification, evidence capture, analysis, and reporting into one workspace. Nettle helps insurers complete risk inspections 5x faster and better manage risks across the policy lifecycle. Underwriters get more timely and higher quality data, while risk engineers focus on the risks where their expertise matters most. Nettle already works with insurers including Allianz and Brotherhood Mutual across Europe, the US, and Asia. Initially built for Commercial Property, the platform has expanded to cover all other lines including Liability, Construction, and Workers’ Compensation. Having helped risk engineers complete inspections 5x faster, Nettle is now extending the same technology to agents and policyholders, allowing insurers to collect risk data on sites they previously could not economically inspect. Nettle will use the funding to expand across the US and Europe, and grow its engineering and go-to-market teams. Built for enterprise insurers, Nettle supports cloud and on-premise deployment, regional data residency, and enterprise-grade security. Nettle was founded in 2024 by former QuantumBlack colleagues Jack Miller and Katya Kinane, who previously built and deployed AI products across insurance and financial services at McKinsey. Katya Kinane, CTO & Co-founder, and Jack Miller, CEO & Co-founder More data. Better decisions. Loss Control used to be constrained by the number of risk engineers an insurer employed. Nettle removes that constraint. Its AI workspace helps insurers collect and understand physical-risk evidence across far more of their portfolios, while reserving scarce engineering expertise for the most complex risks. Identify risk remotely: AI and external data surface potential exposures before anyone visits a site. Democratize data capture: Guided inspections enable risk engineers, agents, and policyholders to collect consistent risk data. Analyze evidence automatically: Nettle analyzes images, video, audio, documents and, third-party data. Turn evidence into decisions: Reports, risk scores, and recommendations that previously took days can be produced in seconds, helping customers get instant insights for faster decision-making. Jack Miller, Nettle co-founder and CEO, comments: Nettle has built a platform that turns Loss Control into a competitive advantage. The purpose has always been to prevent losses, but insurers can only act on the risks they understand. Too often, that understanding is limited by the capacity of their teams, and that’s the ceiling we’re removing. Our AI workspace gives insurers the tools to bring more of the portfolio into view, either through risk engineers, agents, or even policyholders. This round lets us take what we’ve proven across three continents, with extremely positive feedback, and scale it everywhere our customers operate. Kevin McLoughlin, Founder and Managing Partner at MTech, adds: Nettle has built a next-generation platform for risk engineers in their assessment of site risk for large commercial customers. Using generative AI, top global insurers are adopting the Nettle platform, which requires minimal integration effort, to transform physical data collection and analyses for large commercial risks. We are very impressed with Nettle's success to date and the deep experience the founders bring to an area of insurance often overlooked by start-ups. About Nettle Nettle is the AI workspace for Loss Control. Its platform combines remote risk identification, guided inspections, mobile evidence analysis, and instant report generation, helping insurers complete inspections 5x faster and better understand risk across their portfolio. Founded in 2024, Nettle is present in London and New York City. It is backed by MTech, Project A Ventures, Sure Valley Ventures, Portfolio Ventures, and Ventures Together. For more information, visit www.getnettle.com . About MTech MTech is a venture capital firm backing AI-driven companies reshaping insurance and financial services, investing at the early stage across North America and Europe. Founded in 2018 by Kevin and Brian McLoughlin, the firm is backed by some of the world's largest insurance companies and takes a hands-on approach with founders, drawing on decades of combined fintech, venture, and insurance investment banking experience. MTech's portfolio includes Akur8, Covr, Matic, Openly, and Polly. Allianz Türkiye today announced it has selected the Nettle platform to power its commercial property risk engineering operations. The decision follows a pilot programme that demonstrated an up to threefold improvement in the speed at which Allianz Türkiye's risk engineering team can complete property inspections and return structured outputs to underwriters. The deployment addresses a longstanding operational challenge in commercial property insurance: risk engineers completing site visits faster than the downstream reporting process can keep up with. Backlogs build up, underwriters wait for data, and clients receive guidance later than the business needs. Nettle eliminates that bottleneck. Using the Nettle mobile application, built and operating natively in Turkish, Allianz Türkiye's risk engineers leverage agentic AI for preparation and then capture inspection data in the field through photographs, documents, and audio notes. The platform processes all inputs automatically and generates structured inspection reports, risk scores, and underwriter guidance on the same day as the site visit. There is no manual write-up, removing the delay between field and desk. "When I first saw what was possible, my reaction was wow. Nettle is genuinely shaping the future of risk engineering. This is the future for the whole sector, not just Allianz Türkiye." Dr. Ceyhun Eren | Director of Allianz Teknik & Risk Engineering, Allianz Türkiye Ceyhun Eren leads risk engineering at Allianz Türkiye, one of Türkiye's largest and most established multi-line insurers and part of the global Allianz Group. His team operates across a commercial property portfolio spanning a wide range of asset classes and risk profiles. The Nettle platform will be rolled out across the full operation, with underwriters set to receive same-day structured inputs from field inspections for the first time. Allianz Türkiye's decision to deploy Nettle reflects more than a technology upgrade. The company has a long track record of leading risk prevention innovation in Türkiye. Allianz Teknik, established by Allianz Türkiye, is the first and only accredited earthquake and fire test and training centre in the country. That heritage of building infrastructure others follow shapes how the organisation approaches new technology: not as a fast follower, but as a pioneer. Ceyhun and his team came to this with the expertise and the conviction to shape what AI-powered risk engineering should look like, at precisely the moment the industry needed someone to go first." Jack Miller | CEO and Co-Founder, Nettle The Nettle platform works across the full commercial risk assessment workflow, from desktop submission through on-site inspection to underwriter decision. Allianz Türkiye's commitment represents one of the most significant investments in AI-powered risk engineering in the market and a signal of where the broader industry is heading. Othon 6mo Edited Report this post We wanted to better keep track of our deals and how well qualified they were, so I vibe coded a small tool to help us. At nettle , we run weekly deal reviews to make sure we're on top of our pipeline and forecasting is accurate. We use MEDDPICC to make sure we're doing all the right things. But it's a lot of information, across a lot of deals, and sometimes some things might get missed. So I built us a 3-screen tool that shows us: 1. a RAG system showing where each of our Qualified deals is according to MEDDPICC criteria, 2. a timeline to see when they're closing so we can better allocate resources, and 3. an outbound tracking dashboard that shows how our different campaigns are performing. To get the right context on the deals, I’ve got a Python script that pulls data via APIs from: 1. our main sales-related Slack channels, 2. our CRM (Attio), and 3. our Linear project management board. A Claude Sonnet 4.5 API (Opus costs would be crazy) then processes all the information to build the narrative that goes on the dashboard. Building this took around 5 hours on Claude Code, especially with a lot of tweaking and learning about what's the right level of context + what are the right prompts to deliver a useful narrative. For instance, I’ve learned that there is literally no need to use the latest sales call(s) as input, as they’re very token-heavy and can be substituted for a handful of sentences on that call. This is run automatically once a week, which costs way less than a dollar, and we have a much clearer idea of where our pipeline is, and where gaps may be. Every time it's run, a Slack message is fired to our main sales channel providing the headline numbers, WoW change, and any risks. Super fun project, and I'm now looking forward to continuing to work on a bigger one, where I'm building a self-recursive agent to do market research that feeds into our cold outbound. Othon 4mo Report this post We used to spend hours filling out vendor questionnaires. Now, it's just a few minutes mostly reviewing answers. Every client engagement comes with one. The questions are ~80% the same, just worded differently. The format – Excel, Word, sometimes a scored risk assessment – varies each time, which was the real time sink, even with Claude's help. So I built a skill in Cowork that fills them in. In the last few weeks, it: - Filled a 50-question AI security assessment that came as a multi-sheet Excel, dropdowns and all. - Was able to handle a totally new form layout without breaking. - Drafted a follow-up clarification reply off the same answer bank. How does it work? The setup is just a folder in Google Drive: - a SKILL.md that tells Cowork how to match and fill, - an answer bank CSV with vetted answers built from previous answered forms, - a couple of Python scripts to help read and write Excel and Word, and - Markdown files to help answer in the customer's own vocabulary. We kick it off with a simple prompt, in the comments. Every answer is reviewed by a human who owns it before it goes out. After each form is completed, new questions get reconciled back into the bank, so the next form is faster than the last.
